title: The Man Who Planted Trees
description: A dead plateau, an empty flask, and a shepherd who says almost nothing and plants a hundred acorns a day. You are the Traveller, twenty when you first climb up to his lamp and fifty at the end: you saw one man silently bring dead land back to life — what will you do with what you saw? Stay beside him and give it your life, or go your way and come back once a year? Name him, so that the forest is his and guarded, or keep the silence he lives by, though a forest that is nobody's gets cut?
line: One man, a hundred acorns a day — and thirty years in which you decide where your life is and whose the forest will be.
source: after the story by Jean Giono
